item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
189
ABPZ20 KNHC 262353
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Mon Oct 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles south-southwest of
Manzanillo, Mexico, and on Tropical Depression Olana, located
several hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 270231
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026
 
...VANCE DRIFTS WESTWARD AND WEAKENS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.5N 106.3W
ABOUT 275 MI...445 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 340 MI...550 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern and west-central coasts of Mexico
should monitor the progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 15.5 North, longitude 106.3 West. Vance is
moving toward the west near 5 mph (7 km/h). A turn to the northwest
is expected on Tuesday, followed by a northward turn on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next few 
days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4 
inches of rain, with isolated higher totals of 7 inches possible, 
across southern Sinaloa, southwest Durango, and coastal sections of 
Nayarit and Jalisco.   This rainfall may produce flooding and 
mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance, 
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic 
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of
southern, southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 270231
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 PM MST Mon Oct 26 2026
 
The structure of Vance has degraded significantly over the last 
several hours as the center of the cyclone has become separated from 
the convection as seen on visible satellite imagery. Based on a 
combination of the subjective and objective intensity estimates, the 
initial intensity has been lowered to 45 kt. 
 
Vance has continued to move slowly to the west, 275/4 kt. The 
tropical storm is expected to make a turn to west-northwest or 
northwest over the next 24 h due to a weak mid-level ridge to the 
north of the system. By Wednesday, a broad mid-level trough near the 
Baja California Peninsula should force Vance to turn more to the 
north. The current NHC track forecast remains in good agreement with 
the most recent GDMI and HCCA models. There is still some model 
spread in the latter portion of the track forecast, however the 
current track still favors a more slower storm motion overall. 

Strong westerly to southwesterly wind shear is expected to persist 
and increase through the forecast period. However, given the 
presence of warm water and sufficient atmospheric moisture, the 
cyclone is currently forecast to weaken only gradually over the next 
several days. The intensity forecast remains on the upper end of the 
guidance and brings Vance to a post-tropical cyclone around 72 
hours, as the convection will likely be sheared off by the 
aforementioned trough by that time. It should be noted that it is 
possible the system could degenerate into a remnant low sooner than 
currently forecast, however, GFS and ECMWF simulated satellite 
guidance indicates that intermittent convective bursts could still 
occur near the center during the next few days.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact 
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall 
may produce flooding and mudslides across southern Sinaloa, 
southwest Durango, and coastal sections of Nayarit and Jalisco, 
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
2. Interests in southwest and west-central Mexico should 
continue to monitor Vance's progress.
